score_notes.A: Clean Jekyll markup: no body H1, no skipped levels, $$ only, fenced code, real tables, subtitle/paper_author/paper_doi, two-level categories. Deductions: L581 '### 정리: 정책과 보상 사이의 대응' (paper-conclusion recap) is nested inside the OOD/GPT-4 section rather than the closing; L35-59 reads as an intro/contributions recap after the TL;DR ('L55 저자들이 주장하는 기여는 다음과 같습니다').
score_notes.B: Natural 입니다 register held throughout, terms consistent (브래들리-테리, 분배 함수, 암묵적 보상). Deductions: repeated frames 'L180 이 상쇄가 미묘한 이유는' / 'L399 이 해석이 미묘한 이유는', 'L192 이유가 여기에 있습니다' / 'L401 근거가 여기에 있습니다'; formulaic 'L142 이 유도에서 놓치기 쉬운 점이 있습니다.'; calque 'L53 암묵적 보상에 대한 최적 정책' (-> '암묵적 보상의 최적 정책'); frequent '즉' restatements (L51, L134, L377, L395, L417, L488).
score_notes.C: Concepts precede use; '앞서' back-references are accurate; the 0.5/0.3/0.2 toy carries through L146, L160, L369. Deductions: L441 and L443 say the same thing in adjacent paragraphs; L583 conclusion recap interrupts the evaluator section.
score_notes.D: Hard steps get strong help at the right moment (L146 closed-form toy, L160 reward recovery, L194 loss magnitude, L246-254 weight table, L369 projection check, L429 baseline-variance example). Deductions for padding the easy: L97 KL definition, L322 equivalence-relation axioms with a mod-3 example, L504 sampling-temperature definition, L565 inter-annotator agreement definition.
score_notes.E: Code verbatim from the paper (L283-308), tables verbatim (L554-557, L567-575 incl. 272/122/199 and '-'), figures referred to descriptively. Deduction: L528-534 two Best-of-N figures introduced with near-identical one-liners ('다음은 ... 그래프입니다', '같은 비교를 ... 그래프입니다') and never read.
score_notes.F: All 15 sampled claims supported; no wrong number, sign, or formula found (gradient weight sigma(r(y_l)-r(y_w)) consistent at L25, L241, L244, L262; |V|^L at L150). Deductions: L563 '자원봉사자 25명입니다' omits that one late volunteer was excluded from the analysis (App. D.3); L587 '데이터가 SFT 분포와 다른 정책에서 생성되었을 때 결과가 얼마나 유지되는지는 검증되지 않았습니다' overstates — TL;DR preferences came from a different SFT model and HH responses from an unknown LM (Sec. 6), so the paper partly exercises that setting.
